questions.question: Why is `const o: Opts = { timeout: 1, retries: 3 }` an error when `Opts` is `{ timeout: number }`, while assigning a variable holding the same object is not?
options: Excess property checks apply only to fresh object literals
The variable is widened to any
questions.explanation: Structural typing allows extra properties in general. Excess property checking is a special rule for fresh literals, where an extra key is probably a typo.

questions.question: Under `strictFunctionTypes`, if Dog extends Animal, which assignment between function-typed properties is allowed?
options: A `(d: Dog) => void` assigned to `(a: Animal) => void`
A `(a: Animal) => void` assigned to `(d: Dog) => void`
questions.explanation: Parameters are contravariant: a handler for any Animal can safely handle a Dog, but not the reverse.

questions.question: Which strict-mode program compiles but fails at runtime because of a deliberate soundness hole?
options: `const dogs: Dog[] = [new Dog()]; const animals: Animal[] = dogs; animals.push(new Cat()); dogs[1].bark();`
questions.explanation: Mutable arrays are treated as covariant, so a Cat can be pushed into what is really a Dog[]. The other options are compile errors.

questions.question: Why does `Object.keys(obj)` return `string[]` instead of `(keyof typeof obj)[]`?
options: Because of a bug that was never fixed
Because structural typing lets an object have more keys at runtime than its type lists
Because Object.keys is not typed in the standard lib
questions.explanation: A value typed as { x; y } may carry extra keys (width subtyping), so promising only keyof T would be unsound.
